Switch Debouncing Using SR Latch: Step by Step Operation

Switch debouncing using SR latch needs a single pole double throw switch and two cross coupled NAND gates. The common contact is grounded, and each throw connects to one latch input that is held high by a pull up resistor. Because NAND latch inputs are active low, a low on S sets the output Q high and a low on R resets it.

S (active low)R (active low)Q outputMeaning
011Contact touching the set side, output set
100Contact touching the reset side, output reset
11No changeContact in the air or bouncing, output holds
00Not allowedCannot happen with a changeover switch

Sequence when the button is pressed

  1. At rest the contact sits on R, so R is low and Q is 0.
  2. When pressed, the contact leaves R. Both inputs are now high, so Q holds 0.
  3. The contact first strikes S. S goes low and Q switches to 1 at once.
  4. The contact bounces off S. Both inputs return high, which is the hold state, so Q stays 1.
  5. The bouncing contact never travels back far enough to reach R, so no false reset occurs.
  6. On release the same process happens in reverse, giving one clean falling edge.

The latch reacts on the first touch, so there is no added delay, which is why this method suits clock inputs and lab trainers. Its limitation is that it cannot work with ordinary two terminal push buttons.
